findings.issue: Ambiguous. "Nothing was ever reported" reads as "nobody flagged the problem" rather than "nobody submitted a balance for that account." It also repeats the "0.00 + contradiction" shape of reel 002 ("0.00 March totals zero. The GL says otherwise."), which is the second hook in the set led by 0.00.
findings.fix: Rewrite the body so it names the missing balance, and consider a lead other than 0.00 so it doesn't echo 002. Something in the shape of "0.00 / but nobody sent a balance" or move away from the number lead entirely.

findings.issue: 2100 is an account number, not a row number. On a sheet that shows real row numbers 1-10 down the gutter, calling it "Row 2100" invites a double take.
findings.fix: "Acct 2100 has no amount." (22 chars, still inside the limit).

findings.issue: The function is never named out loud. "Test the result first" and "print something a person can read" describe the idea but a viewer can't repeat it. IF only appears in payoff.sub.
findings.fix: Name it: "So wrap it in IF. If the lookup comes back empty, print something a person can read."

findings.issue: "zero is a number your owner will believe" is off for the stated audience and "your owner" is an odd possessive. Also the payoff VO and payoff.headline carry slightly different ideas.
findings.fix: Tighten to something a controller would text: "An empty source cell comes back as a real zero, and a zero gets signed off."

findings.issue: Three lines where prior payoffs land in one or two ("VLOOKUP COUNTS COLUMNS", "TRIM WON'T TOUCH CHAR 160"). "EVERY TIME" adds nothing.
"Says so on the page" is a stiff construction nobody says.
findings.fix: "Wrap the lookup in IF so an empty source cell shows as empty, not as a balance."

hook.note: Real symptom, concrete, short, and it is a close-week experience: an account shows 0.00 because nobody submitted a balance. Loses a point for the ambiguous second clause and for being the second hook in the set fronted by 0.00.

claims.claim: VLOOKUP against an empty source cell returns 0
claims.note: Exact-match VLOOKUP pointing at a blank cell returns 0, and the #,##0.00 format displays it as 0.00. Matches the verified expected value.

claims.claim: "Nothing's missing here. VLOOKUP found the row."
claims.note: A2 = 2100 matches A8, so no #N/A. The reel correctly separates "no match" from "match with empty cell," which is the whole point.

claims.claim: VLOOKUP(...)="" is TRUE when the looked-up cell is empty
claims.note: Excel treats the empty-cell result as equal to "" in that comparison. Consistent with the verified "No data" output.

claims.claim: "A real zero in the export still shows as zero"
claims.note: 0="" evaluates FALSE in Excel, so a genuine 0 falls through to the second VLOOKUP and prints 0.00. Not shown on screen, but the statement is correct.
IF and VLOOKUP with a nested duplicate lookup work in 2016/2019 and 365. No dynamic arrays, no LET, no IFERROR-only behaviour.

claims.claim: Data realism (accts 2100/2150/2400, 3,120.00 / 1,045.00, accrued liability recon vs trial balance export)
claims.note: Plausible accrued-liability range and non-round amounts. Reads like a real close recon against a TB export.
Blank source cell returning zero, and one fix for it. Nothing about #N/A handling or IFERROR creeps in.
First line "vlookup returns 0 instead of blank" is a real search phrase, 5 hashtags, CTA limited to "save this." No Steda or consulting mention anywhere.
